findings.title: isAccessTokenId uses wrong substring and inverted check
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the encoded prefix, so it is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. On top of that, the matcher returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Taken together, the matcher accepts token IDs whose grant type is wrong and would reject a correctly encoded one. The grant-type assertions in the event tests are therefore meaningless.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` was meant to check `rawTokenId`, as its message says. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and encoding then produces IDs like `onrtac:null`.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut validation is incomplete; custom grants can break token issuance
findings.body: The size comparison misses collisions, for example two grants sharing a shortcut while another pair collides on ID. Shortcuts are also never checked to be exactly 2 characters, yet the decoder requires a 6-character prefix. A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returning a 3-letter shortcut (the interface javadoc even suggests 3 letters) yields token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects. A factory returning null from `getShortcut` makes ConcurrentHashMap throw an NPE at startup. Adding `getShortcut()` as an abstract method also breaks every existing third-party grant factory at compile time; a default implementation would avoid that.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The public copy constructor of `OAuth2GrantType.Context` was deleted. Extensions or subclasses that use it will no longer compile. It should be kept, with the new `grantType` field also copied.

findings.title: Unregistered grant type string makes token creation throw
findings.body: A flow can set `GRANT_TYPE` to a value with no registered factory. Examples are a disabled feature or a custom provider such as PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType when its feature toggles at runtime. In that case `encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` and access token issuance fails. Falling back to the unknown (`na`) shortcut would avoid the outage.
